title: Milky Way
body:
The **Milky Way** is the galaxy containing the Sun. It is a barred spiral roughly 100,000
light-years across, with the Sun about 27,000 light-years from the centre, orbiting once every
230 million years.

Mapping it is difficult from the inside, which is the point worth appreciating. Everything is
seen in projection along a line of sight, and dust in the disc blocks visible light toward the
centre, so the structure was assembled from radio and infrared observations that pass through
the dust, combined with distances measured star by star.

Its structure divides into a disc holding the spiral arms, young stars and the gas they form
from, a central bulge and bar of older stars, and a halo of old globular clusters extending far
beyond the disc.

The **rotation curve** is where the surprise appears. Orbital speed should fall with distance
from the centre once most of the mass is enclosed, which is what the planets do around the Sun.
Measured speeds, from the [[Doppler Effect]] applied to gas in the disc, stay flat far
past the visible edge:

```
expected:   speed falls as 1/√r beyond the visible mass
measured:   speed stays roughly constant to the limit of detection
```

Something with mass and no light extends well past the stars, which is the main evidence for
[[Dark Matter]].
